subject: Network assertion + CI fallback plan for Nimbus on-prem rollout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Benson <sara.benson@nimbus-energy.com>, infra@nimbus-energy.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Network assertion + CI fallback plan for Nimbus on-prem rollout

Hi Sara / Nimbus infra team,

Following our architecture session yesterday, attached is a concise test plan and a small terraform diff that implements our network-assertion hooks during bootstrap. Key asks: can your ops team confirm the egress test ranges and our ability to run the assertion agent in a pre-network namespace before route propagation?

High-level flow we want to land in the repo:
- Terraform module: add a preflight null_resource that triggers the "network-assertion" job (see patch). The job runs the assertion container and emits structured JSON results to S3-compatible storage.
- Helm: a templated Job that can run as a one-off in the customer cluster for KV/cache connectivity checks. Values examples attached.
- Ansible: post-provision playbook runs to reconcile any host-level firewall rules (we've kept this minimal).
- CI gating: master branch must pass the network-assertion smoke before merging a private-deploy plan; if assertion fails we want an automated fallback that:
  * aborts the plan and runs a light rollback of network changes,
  * flips traffic to a temporary egress proxy (mirror mode) for validation,
  * notifies both Redwood and Nimbus ops with a runbook link.

Attached: network-assertion-testplan.md, terraform-module-diff.patch, helm-values-examples.yaml.

Deliverables and owners:
- Nimbus: confirm assertion ranges and ability to run an ephemeral job in pre-route state (Sara) — needed by EOD Friday.
- Redwood infra: wire CI job + fallback playbook (Monica / Marissa).
- Runbook: draft attached as ci-fallback-playbook.pdf (internal) — we will iterate after your confirmation.

We want to avoid manual troubleshooting during the first wave of on-prem rollouts; this gating + fallback should keep us safe without long escalations.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-assertion-testplan.md (text), terraform-module-diff.patch (patch), helm-values-examples.yaml (yaml)
From: Sara Benson <sara.benson@nimbus-energy.com>

Cc: infra@nimbus-energy.com, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network assertion + CI fallback plan for Nimbus on-prem rollout

Karthik / team,

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments — I've skimmed the test plan and the Terraform patch. A few notes from Nimbus ops:
- We can run ephemeral jobs during bootstrap but need them to run with a service account that has only network-read permissions; will not allow broad egress during that phase.
- Egress ranges: 52.23.10.0/24 and 34.102.0.0/20 (these are our NAT ranges for mgmt plane). Please bake those into the assertion config.
- The idea of flipping to an egress proxy mirror is fine, but we need to see the failure thresholds (timeouts and error rates) that trigger the switch.

I'm attaching our internal network policy PDF that details the approved processes and the procurement approval path for enabling ephemeral test egress. We'll need that approval before we allow the assertion job to actually make external calls.

I'll coordinate with procurement if we need to sign the exception. If Redwood can show the assertion runs with restricted egress (metadata-only checks) we can probably avoid the approval step.

Sara Benson
Head of IT Operations, Nimbus Energy
Attachments: nimbus-network-policy.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Benson <sara.benson@nimbus-energy.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network assertion + CI fallback plan for Nimbus on-prem rollout

Thanks Sara — that egress CIDR list and the restricted SA constraint are actionable. Quick internal notes and proposed changes:

1) CI job placement
- We'll add a dedicated job in the priv-deploy pipeline named "net-assertion-smoke". It runs as an independent stage before terraform apply. If it fails, the pipeline triggers the fallback stage (see 3).

2) Test variants
- metadata-only: checks DNS, service account access to API, and kubelet auth (no external egress) — this avoids procurement.
- full-egress: runs actual external reachability tests — gated by a manual approval step (Nimbus confirms).

3) Fallback playbook (draft)
- ci-fallback-playbook.pdf (attached): steps to revert the terraform change by running the reverse plan (we'll keep plans immutable so rollback is deterministic). It then deploys an egress-proxy helm chart in mirror-mode (no production traffic) and re-runs net-assertion against mirrored traffic. If mirrored assertions pass, we surface results to ops and open JIRA-INF-1729 for follow-up.

4) Helm/Ansible changes
- Helm values will include a flag `assertion.enabled` and `assertion.mode: metadata|egress` so Nimbus can choose metadata-only runs during procurement.
- Ansible will have a dry-run mode to verify host firewall state without mutating during the assertion step.

I'll push a short PR to the infra repo with the job and the helm values examples by EOD. Monica and David — can one of you own the PR and CI wiring?

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Staff Engineer, Deployment Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ci-fallback-playbook.pdf, helm-values-examples.yaml

Thanks everyone — agreed on plan and next steps. Short summary of decisions for the record:
- Implement two assertion modes (metadata-only and full-egress). Nimbus will start with metadata-only to avoid procurement gating.
- CI: add net-assertion-smoke stage; failures trigger ci-fallback-playbook which runs reverse terraform plan and deploys egress-proxy in mirror-mode.
- Rollback window default: 10 minutes (David to own).
- Sara: we'll incorporate your CIDRs and SA restriction into the assertion config; please confirm the CIDRs in a follow-up if anything changes.

Next action owners:
- Marissa: PR + helm values + playbook updates (due EOD Friday).
- David: pipeline wiring + rollback step (PR by Monday).
- Monica: coordinate with Nimbus procurement if we need the full-egress approval path (monitor).

I'll open JIRA-INF-1729 with the acceptance criteria and link the drive folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cDriveSharedLink

If Sara's team is OK with metadata-only runs we can begin the repo changes this week and schedule the first dry-run in a staging cluster next Wednesday.

Cheers,
Karthik

Senior Manager, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
